newsitem.title: UK: GOLF-WOODS PLUS FOUR FOR THE OPEN TITLE.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-WOODS PLUS FOUR FOR THE OPEN TITLE.

text.p: The talent and ability that Tiger Woods has shown in abundance will be given an exacting test at the British Open over the windy Royal Troon course this week.
And if Woods is not up to the demands of one of the toughest layouts in the Open rota, there are four other players at the top of their games ready to launch assaults on the title.

Ernie Els, Greg Norman, Colin Montgomerie and Tom Lehman have all presented their credentials as championship candidates with victories over the past month and any of them could prevail if Woods is not at the absolute peak of his game.

But everything revolves around Woods in golf these days, ever since he turned professional last summer and won the first of the seven victories that boosted him to the world number one position in only 42 weeks.

The pinnacle of his achievements thus far was the Masters at Augusta in April, where at 21 he became the youngest ever champion with a record 12-shot victory over a course that has historically been one of the toughest in the world.
"He has the game throttled," Nick Faldo said later.
Since then he has captured the Byron Nelson Classic and the Western Open.

But there have been other tournaments where he was less than superhuman, especially last month's U.S. Open at the Congressional Club where he struggled against the narrow fairways and dense rough before finishing joint 19th.
He does, however, come to Troon on the heels of his latest victory at the Western Open 10 days ago.
But the Scottish course with its narrow, bouncy fairways, variable rough and small greens should provide a supreme test, especially if the wind blows as has been forecast.
In those conditions, he may have to shelve his normal high-flying drives in favour of lower-trajectory shots that are less affected by the wind.
He has been working on the change in consultation with his coach, Butch Harmon, and how effective he is at hitting lower shots may be the key to his chance of success here.
Els has risen up the rankings to number two in the world on the strength of his second U.S. Open triumph last month, where he beat Montgomerie by one shot and Lehman by two on a pulsating final day.
Montgomerie, who played with him, most admires Els's calmness under pressure and if the giant South African gets off to a good start, he will take some catching.
Els took two weeks off after his U.S. Open triumph and returned to competition at last week's Loch Lomond World Invitational where after a slow start he climbed up to second place by the end.

Norman, the 1986 and 1993 Open champion now world-ranked third after being number one for 313 weeks at various times, underlined his form with his success in the St Jude Classic in Memphis at the end of June.
He credits Faldo's coach, David Leadbetter. "My game has really gone up a notch or two over the last six or eight weeks," he said on Tuesday.
Montgomerie's claim for his first taste of major championship form stems from his close finish to Els last month and his subsequent victory in the Irish Open, where he closed with a superb 62.
Lehman comes in as the holder, fresh from an impressive five-stroke victory over Els at Loch Lomond where Norman and Montgomerie also played.
Norman rates Lehman as being a keen contender after that victory.
"Most of the time we come in here without playing the week before. For Tom to go there and win the way he played and then come here and defend, he's bringing some momentum with him."

Nick Price, the 1994 champion, feels he is doing everything well and just needs any one of several departments of his game to be brilliant to have a good chance of a repeat on the course where he threw away the Open in 1982.
Price led by three shots with six holes to play that year, but dropped four shots to let in Tom Watson.
Faldo has won the Open three times to go with his three Masters titles but does not seem to be firing on all cylinders now.
Neither is the American challenge is not as strong as usual and tapers off after Woods and Lehman with such former contenders as Corey Pavin and Fred Couples in a slump.
